summary.headline: Ksolves Q2 FY27 revenue fell 4.7% YoY to INR 37.8 crores on client ramp-downs; EBITDA margin 25.7%, within guided band.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 37.8 crores, down 4.7% YoY and 8.8% QoQ, driven by client-specific ramp-downs at a couple of large enterprise accounts and cautious client spending. EBITDA was INR 9.7 crores at a 25.7% margin (vs 30.3% in Q1 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26), which management attributed to lower revenue partly offset by cost actions and AI-led productivity. PAT was INR 7.25 crores (19.2% margin), and H1 revenue grew 2.5% YoY to INR 79.2 crores. Management guided FY27 revenue to trail FY26 and EBITDA margin to stay within 25-30%, with H2 focus on pipeline building, AI opportunities and enterprise account recovery.

financial_highlights.change: vs 30.3% in Q1 FY27 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26
broadly in line with H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1 per share second interim; H1 total INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT)

segments.name: IT services
segments.commentary: Core business at 98.4% of Q2 revenue. Geography: North America 59%, India 20%, Europe 6%, Australia 4%, rest of world 11%; overseas 80%.

segments.name: BFSI / banking
segments.commentary: Three Q2 wins in banking (South America, UK, Europe). BFSI share of revenue rose from 7% to 8% (H1 FY26 vs H1 FY27 per analyst slide); management says the jump comes from H2. Company has about 11-12 BFSI clients.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 25% of revenue this year vs 27% last year per analyst reading of slides; one telecom client that was closing its business is now re-engaging.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to remain soft and trail FY26 levels; company did not reaffirm earlier guidance.
EBITDA margin expected within the 25%-30% guided range for FY27, with scope for improvement in Q4 as recent wins ramp up; management said margins would be at the upper end if sales traction holds.
Full-quarter benefit of Q2 cost actions expected from end of Q3.
Management said it is optimistic about returning to growth in FY28, with a 20%-plus growth aspiration conditional on geopolitical stability.
Dividend to be decided each year based on profitability and cash needs; shareholder returns remain a priority.
capex_capacity: Headcount fell about 10% from ~550 to ~495; hiring in FY27 limited to 5-10% of last year's level, and capacity is to be filled from the existing team before new hiring.
AI productivity: management says one person can now deliver 2x-3x prior output.

Built a low-code/no-code agent platform for a telecom client used by 500+ operations staff; migrated a US client's legacy codebase with 8 agents in about 7-8 months versus an estimated 1-1.5 years manually.
Opened a sales office in Australia for local bids; delivery team is based in India.
Being a Select Partner in Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI networks; 100% of engineers Claude certified.
demand_pricing: Client spending remains selective and discretionary spend under scrutiny; management said clients had put decisions on hold until around 10 September over AI wait-and-watch, and are now returning with AI-led requirements.
Customers now ask for Odoo, Salesforce or data engineering with agentic AI; management says the sales question has shifted from headcount to business outcome.
Two large enterprise accounts ramped down; management called these client-specific, not structural, and said the pipeline was not deep enough to offset them in the quarter.
Management said some clients tested building in-house AI tools but have since returned to outsourcing projects for features.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividends continue at around 100% of PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder returns remain a priority; the Board will decide each payout based on yearly profitability and cash needs. H1 interim dividend totalled INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT).

qa_highlights.question: Do you have constant-currency numbers given rupee weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the company is not currently calculating revenue in constant currency.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the two clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, but said it was large enough to be a big hit; new Q1 and Q2 wins absorbed much of it, though a deficit remained.

qa_highlights.question: How will the margin move with sales traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would be at the upper end of the guided range if revenue recovers; the INR 3.6 crore revenue drop was the main driver of the Q2 margin dip.

qa_highlights.question: Will the banking wins contribute meaningfully, and how big can BFSI become?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects are underway and take months to quarters; the South American bank relationship is ongoing but expansion is not in writing. Management hopes other banks will follow.

qa_highlights.question: Are you entering cybersecurity?
qa_highlights.answer: Still exploring; management sees AI guardrails and security as a demand opportunity but has not defined the offering.

risks_watch: Revenue trend: FY27 guided soft, with dependence on recovery at re-engaged accounts and on H2 BFSI wins converting into revenue.
Margin: Q2 margin fell to 25.7% from 30.3% in Q1; watch whether cost actions hold the 25-30% band as revenue recovers.
Client concentration: top 10 clients are 50% of revenue, and two large accounts ramped down in Q2.
Currency: management does not track constant-currency revenue despite a weaker rupee, so FX effect on reported numbers is not visible.
Management did not reaffirm prior guidance; new cybersecurity vertical is still undefined.
summary.management_tone: Candid but guarded: management called the quarter mixed and attributed the decline to client-specific ramp-downs, while staying confident about AI wins and a FY28 recovery. Answers on FY28 growth and client-level revenue were conditional or unquantified, and the company declined to give lost-revenue figures.
key_quotes: These are client -specific ramp -down, not a structural change in our business or our client relationship.
So simply put, this was a revenue -led dip.
We are now building a pipeline, even a strong pipeline enough that no client-specific decision can move our quarter the way this one did.
Ksolves is putting agentic AI into production for paying clients, not just running pilots.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to trail FY26 (guidance cut, earlier guide not reaffirmed), with EBITDA margin held at 25-30%; backing is cost actions, AI productivity and pipeline recovery with no specific capacity, orders or contracts quantified, so backing is vague.
